summary: Wildlife cinematographer Sophie Darlington answers readers' questions about making the National Geographic documentary Lion, which followed one cub for four years as it grew up on the African savanna. She talks about breaking into wildlife filmmaking, how she gets close-up safari shots, and the hardest moments of the project.
title: A Filmmaker on What it Takes to Spend Four Years With Lions
Can This Bone-Eating Bird Be Saved?
summary: In South Africa, Shannon Hoffman runs a breeding program racing to save the critically endangered African bearded vulture. Her team gathers eggs from wild nests in the Drakensberg mountains and raises the chicks with puppet feeding, hoping their offspring can one day be released back into the wild.
caption: A bone for me, an egg for tomorrow
alt: A rust-orange bearded vulture with a cream face and bristly black beard perches on a rock below snowy mountains, beside a small bone and a speckled egg in a nest.
